# Overview

The Canadian Postsecondary Education Alcohol and Drug Use Survey
(CPADS) is a Health Canada survey whose public-use microdata file
(PUMF) is open data. rmorie provides a *canonical* column contract and
`morie_canonicalize_cpads_data()`, which maps the raw PUMF columns to
analysis-ready names.

The examples use the synthetic CPADS frame that ships with rmorie: it
has the PUMF's columns but random values, so the numbers below are not
findings about students. The real PUMF loads the same way (see
"Loading the real PUMF").

# The CPADS column contract

```{r contract}
library(rmorie)
contract <- morie_cpads_contract()
contract$required_variables
unlist(contract$raw_column_map)
```

`morie_cpads_contract()` returns the canonical variable names, the raw
PUMF column each comes from, and notes on the source. Using the
contract is opt-in: the estimators in rmorie do not require it.

# Loading and canonicalising

```{r load}
raw <- morie_datasets_cpads(offline = TRUE)
dim(raw)
df <- morie_canonicalize_cpads_data(raw)

# Returns the names of required canonical columns that are missing
# (character(0) when all are present); with strict = TRUE, the
# default, it stops instead.
morie_validate_cpads_data(df)
```

# Survey-weighted proportions

The PUMF weight is mapped to the canonical column `weight`. A weighted
proportion of heavy drinking in the past 30 days among respondents
with a non-missing answer:

```{r analysis}
ok <- !is.na(df$heavy_drinking_30d)
stats::weighted.mean(df$heavy_drinking_30d[ok], df$weight[ok])
mean(df$heavy_drinking_30d[ok])          # unweighted, for comparison
```

# Propensity-score IPW workflow

`morie_run_propensity_ipw_analysis()` estimates the effect of a binary
treatment on a binary outcome (by default `cannabis_any_use` on
`heavy_drinking_30d`) with a logistic propensity model and trimmed
inverse-probability weights. It requires the `weight` column but does
not apply the survey weights in the estimate:

```{r causal}
ipw <- morie_run_propensity_ipw_analysis(df)
ipw$ipw_results
ipw$diagnostics
```

# Loading the real PUMF

```{r real, eval = FALSE}
raw_real <- morie_load_dataset("ocp21")
df_real  <- morie_canonicalize_cpads_data(raw_real)
dim(df_real)
# 40931   403
```

This chunk is not run when the vignette is built, because the first
call downloads the PUMF from open.canada.ca.
